answer: Each agent claims one timber bay of a bridge deck, locks 70 credits, and posts cable tension and sag plus the fable code on its timber plank. A cable table lets a bridge auditor recompute sag from tension and load. The first claim pays 33 credits; the kth pays 33+7(k-1), so the 1000th pays 7026 and 1000 fakes pay 3,529,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-cable ring reusing another bay's readings fails because tension, sag, and fable code must match that bay's entry; mismatch, missing data, or duplicate code burns the bond. An honest agent pays 33 once and recovers the bond after a passed epoch.
